# Sada (صدى)

> Sada is an Arabic-first, fully offline speech-to-text desktop app for Windows. It is an
> independent fork of Vibe v3.2.2 (MIT) with a complete Arabic (ar-IQ) interface, RTL layout,
> Arabic transcription defaults, Arabic transcript normalization (including Latin technical-term
> restoration) and Arabic PDF export. Audio never
> leaves the machine. No telemetry, no updater, no account, no phone relay. Since 3.3.0 the same
> executable is a local MCP server, so AI agents can transcribe Arabic audio and read saved
> transcripts over stdio with no port and no network.

## Key facts

- Name: Sada (صدى) — "echo"
- Version: 3.10.0
- Platform: Windows 10/11 x64 (Tauri 2 desktop app)
- License: MIT (fork of Vibe v3.2.2, MIT); bundled FFmpeg is GPLv3 (mere aggregation, see notices)
- Engine: whisper.cpp via the bundled `vibe-server` sidecar (v0.6.16; built by Sada from
  `server/` as `v0.6.16-sada.1`, adding a loopback Host/Origin guard); models are NOT bundled
- Installers (v3.10.0, GitHub Releases, unsigned, per-user `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Sada\`):
  `Sada_3.10.0_x64-setup.exe` (~45 MB, downloads WebView2 at install) and
  `Sada_3.10.0_x64-setup-offline.exe` (~250 MB, embeds the WebView2 installer). The NSIS hook
  installs the VC++ 2015-2022 runtime from Microsoft when missing, so fully offline machines must
  pre-install `vc_redist.x64.exe`
- Managed deployment (since v3.9.0): `Sada_3.10.0_x64_en-US.msi` (per-machine WiX, ~71 MB, admin rights)
  plus a machine-wide policy (HKLM `SOFTWARE\Sada\Policy` / `%ProgramData%\Sada\policy.json`) that
  can enforce offline mode and disable AI, URL import and model downloads; guides in
  `docs/ENTERPRISE-DEPLOYMENT.md` and `docs/NETWORK.md`
- UI and accessibility (v3.10.0): recovery-first error dialog with kind-specific actions,
  copy-all, export grouped into four families, Settings as a header dialog (gear / `Ctrl+,`),
  Arabic tracking and bidi fixes, truth-only trust copy; runtime axe audit over 35 UI states
  found 0 violations. Four Wave-1 repairs only — the 4.0 "Echo" identity is not in this release,
  and a five-user Arabic gate (`docs/design/ui-decisions/GATE-KIT.md`) must pass before Wave 2
- Languages: Arabic `ar-IQ` first; 20+ inherited upstream locales available
- Network: only user-requested actions (model download, pasted URL, optional summary provider);
  the complete egress list is `docs/NETWORK.md`, and offline mode blocks the connectivity probe too
- GPU: optional Vulkan acceleration on NVIDIA/AMD/Intel GPUs, selectable in Settings → Models →
  Hardware; falls back to the CPU automatically and ships no CUDA/ROCm dependency
- MCP server: `Sada.exe --mcp` (stdio, no port) with four tools: `sada_transcribe`,
  `sada_transcripts`, `sada_transcript`, `sada_info`; `sada_info` reports the configured model's
  capabilities (engine, languages, VAD, translation, prompts); Arabic transcription defaults preserved

## For AI agents and researchers

- Source layout: `desktop/` (React + Tauri shell), `i18n/desktop/` (catalogues incl.
  `ar-IQ.json`, 786 keys), `server/` (Rust whisper.cpp sidecar), `docs/`, `site/`.
- Build/test: `chore setup x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`, `cd desktop && pnpm install && pnpm test && pnpm build`.
- Tests: `pnpm test` = vitest (34 files / 207 tests); `cargo test --release` = 120 Rust tests;
  `python -m unittest discover -s benchmarks/arabic-asr/tests` = 62 tests.
- Do not assume the model is included; a `ggml-*.bin` is required at runtime.
- Agent integration: run `Sada.exe --mcp` as a stdio MCP server; no HTTP port is opened. The
  installed agent skill lives at `.claude|.codex/skills/sada/SKILL.md`.
- The fork keeps upstream MIT copyright notices; cite upstream Vibe as well as this repository
  (see `CITATION.cff`).
